# Topology round-trip latency (measured in-cluster)

**Generated by `./hack/benchmark-report`. Do not edit by hand.**

A dummy AI Gateway calls llm-d-sc over gRPC in the two topologies of `tests/HOMELAB.md`:
as a same-Pod sidecar over loopback, and across a ClusterIP Service from a separate Pod.
The two probes are byte-identical apart from `--target`, so the difference between the
result sets is the network path and nothing else. 200 samples each.

| Metric | same-Pod | ClusterIP | Delta |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| cache hit p50 | 0.033 ms | 0.055 ms | +0.022 ms |
| cache hit p95 | 0.047 ms | 0.067 ms | +0.020 ms |
| cache hit p99 | 0.077 ms | 0.102 ms | +0.025 ms |
| cache hit max | 0.236 ms | 0.305 ms | +0.069 ms |
| cache miss p50 | 16.406 ms | 16.838 ms | +0.432 ms |
| cache miss p95 | 17.547 ms | 18.516 ms | +0.969 ms |
| cache miss p99 | 18.363 ms | 19.305 ms | +0.942 ms |
| cache miss max | 20.060 ms | 25.406 ms | +5.346 ms |

## What this says

**Leaving the Pod costs about 22 microseconds.** That is the isolated cost of
the Service path, visible on a cache hit because a hit does no model work. On a cache miss the
same hop is 2.6% of total latency, because the model forward dominates everything else.

**So the sidecar-versus-Service decision is latency-neutral** and should be made on operational
grounds (lifecycle coupling, scaling, blast radius), not on performance. That is a useful result:
the cheaper-looking topology buys nothing measurable.

**The sub-20ms uncached budget is met, with little headroom.** ClusterIP p99 is
19.30 ms against a 20 ms budget, and the observed MAX of
25.41 ms exceeds it. The budget holds at p99 on this hardware and
would not survive a slower node or a CPU limit, which is why the pod-CPU-limit gap is tracked.

Produced on one contributor's homelab and not independently reproduced.

## Where the time actually goes

The server logs its per-stage decomposition (S-080). Measured in-cluster over 132 served
requests:

| Stage | p50 | p99 | Share of a cache miss |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| network, ClusterIP hop | 22 us | - | 0.18% |
| queue, bounded handoff | 2 us | 64 us | 0.02% |
| tokenize | 56 us | 96 us | 0.46% |
| **model forward** | **12.29 ms** | **14.34 ms** | **99.4%** |

**Everything that is not the model is under one percent of latency.** The bounded handoff, the
result cache, the tokenizer, and the Service network path are collectively about 80
microseconds of a 12.3 millisecond request.

Two consequences worth stating plainly:

Optimisation effort belongs in the forward, which means the model, the quantisation, and the
hardware. Tuning the queue, the cache implementation, or the transport cannot produce a
measurable improvement, because there is under 1% available to win.

The architecture's admission control is effectively free. A bounded queue that costs 2
microseconds at p50 is not a latency trade for safety under load; it is safety at no cost.

Note the `total p50` of 1 microsecond against a `forward p50` of 12.29 milliseconds. That is
not an inconsistency: total is recorded for EVERY request and most requests were cache hits,
so its median is a hit while the forward median is necessarily a miss. It is a direct
illustration of the cache doing its job, visible only because the stages are reported as
distributions rather than as means.
